verifications.claim: Beginning in the 2026 season, each MLB team receives two challenges per game to use on ball-strike calls under the new Automated Ball-Strike (ABS) system.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Each team will get two challenges at the start of the game" (R1); "Each team will start the game with two challenges apiece" (R2); "each team gets two challenges per game" (R4); "Teams get two challenges per nine-inning game" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm two challenges per team per game starting in 2026 for ABS ball-strike calls.

verifications.claim: Teams retain their challenge if the call is overturned.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "can keep them if they're successful" (R1); "successful ABS challenges retained? Yes" (R2); "if teams get a challenge correct, they keep it" (R4); "They keep the ones they get right" (R5); "successful challenges retained? Yes" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported across sources: teams retain challenges on successful (overturned) calls.

verifications.claim: Teams lose their challenge if the call stands.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "keep the challenges if they're successful" implies loss if not (R1); "challenge will be lost if the challenge is not overturned" (R2); "The Yankees lost the challenge" (R4); "lose the ones they get wrong" (R5); "only loses its challenge if the umpire’s call is confirmed" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly or directly implied in sources: challenge lost if call stands (not overturned).

verifications.claim: Only the batter, pitcher, or catcher can call for a review by signaling to the umpire immediately after the pitch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "only allowed to be initiated by a pitcher, catcher, or batter... tapping their hat or helmet... immediately after" (R1); "Only the batter, pitcher and catcher... immediate aftermath... tap their cap or helmet" (R2); "Only hitters, pitchers and catchers... tap their helmet or hat... within two seconds" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources precisely match: only batter/pitcher/catcher, signal by tap, immediately after pitch.

verifications.claim: If a team has no challenges left, they receive one new challenge for the 10th inning.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "given an additional challenge if it has none remaining entering the 10th inning" (R1); "extra challenge in the 10th if they are out" (R2); "team that has already used all... will get one challenge for the 10th inning" (R4); "starts the extra inning out of challenges will get one challenge for the 10th inning" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation for extra challenge in 10th if none left.

verifications.claim: Challenges are not allowed if a position player is pitching.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Challenges are not permitted when a position player is pitching" (R2); "When a position player is pitching, challenges are not permitted" (R7); "Challenges are not allowed when a position player is pitching" (R8)

verifications.claim: Prior to 2026, managers were typically allowed one challenge per game.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "each manager is allotted one challenge per game, with additional challenges granted only if the previous one was successful" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: R6 describes pre-2026 instant replay system where managers got one challenge per game (additional if successful), matching 'typically one'.

verifications.claim: Prior to 2026, a second challenge was added if the first was successful.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "additional challenges granted only if the previous one was successful" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: R6 directly states pre-2026 system allowed additional (second) challenge if first successful.

verifications.claim: Data from 2025/2026 testing showed an average of about four to five challenges per game
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "4.2 ABS challenges... Triple-A game in 2025"; "4.1 challenges per game... Spring Training 2025" (R1); "4.1 challenges per game... 2025 spring training" (R7, R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm ~4.1-4.2 challenges per game in 2025 testing (Spring/Triple-A); '2025/2026' slightly broad but data precisely matches 'about four to five' for pre-2026 implementation testing.
